newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index hits new record high.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index hits new record high.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange index on Sunday set a new record high in a long-lived rally that has pushed it up 40 percent so far this year.
It closed on Sunday at 1,905.2 compared with 1,735.8 points at the end of September. The index started the year at 1,360.1.
The index and trading volume and value have been setting almost weekly records in recent months during the short 2-1/2- hour trading sessions five days a week.
Dealers attribute the upward trend to capital flows from neighbouring states, strong mid-year results by listed firms, lack of other local investment vehicles and a strong economy.

Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds run by local firms.
Kuwait is considering opening trade for foreign investors.
Value of traded shares on Sunday was 57.4 percent higher than September's daily average of 41.4 million dinars ($138.5 million).
